messages:
mei: quick heads-up — r3-alpha (int8) bring-up showing locale-specific regressions across a few eval suites. ZH vertical-layout tests BLEU ~3.2 down vs r2-fp16. also seeing weird merges when UR/FA (urdu/persian) bidi text is interleaved with latin placeholders.

sanjay: is this only the int8 build? did you try r3 in fp16?

mei: only int8 so far. r3-fp16 looks fine on our small smoke set. int8 compile path changed kernel selection and tokenizer preproc was rebuilt in the artifact pipeline last week. attaching a tiny token diff as an inline repro.

mei: ```
# source: vertical Chinese sample (line stacked with ideographs)
原
文
：
测试

# r2-fp16 tokenization (expected)
["原文", "：", "测试"]

# r3-int8 tokenization (observed)
["原", "文：", "测试"]
```

tomo: that split of the first char is suspicious — sounds like a tokenizer normalization/regression rather than model decode. which tokenizer version?

mei: tokenizers v0.13.1 -> v0.14.0 bump happened in the packaging step; I pinned earlier but the CI artifact used the new wheel.

liam: also flagging that our detok step in the eval harness switched to preserve-vertical-newline=true recently. could be affecting BLEU since segmentation changed.

zhang: can you paste a UR/FA example? bidi issues are usually about the directional override and punctuation merging.

mei: snippet for mixed UR+latin: "سلام item: قیمت 100$"

# r2-fp16 decode: "سلام item: قیمت 100$"
# r3-int8 decode: "سلا مitem:قیمت100$"

mei: notice spaces removed and latin glued to preceding arabic run.

sanjay: :facepalm: that looks like a grapheme cluster handling change upstream in tokenization library (or a normalization flag). can you run tokenizer.tokenize on both wheels and diff?

mei: running now. will post minimal wheel-bisect results in ~10m.

eval-bot: CI quick-run: r2-fp16 vs r3-int8 on zh-vertical-dev: BLEU -3.2, chrF -0.045, COMET -0.85. small en->ur test shows fluency drop and punctuation merge. full logs -> https://ci.internal/rs/2163456789/artifacts

liam: if it's tokenization, we should expect BLEU to be sensitive. propose quick experiment: run r2 tokenization + r3-int8 model decode (i.e., normalize tokens before model) to see if model alone contributes.

mei: good idea. I'll run hybrid eval (r2 tokenization + r3-int8) and r3-int8 tokenization + r2-fp16 decode to isolate.

deploy-bot: canary r3-alpha-int8 deployed to us-west-canary at 2026-03-20T10:12:14Z (id: canary-2163456789). Traffic routed: 1%.

tomo: if bisect points to tokenizers wheel, we should revert that wheel in the build and re-run quantization compile. quant kernels might be ok.

mei: update — quick bisect shows tokenizers wheel v0.14.0 changes default "separate_cjk" normalization. patch diff: "separate_cjk: false -> true" which explains extra splits. pushing a pinned wheel to canary and kicking another CI run.

eval-bot: quick-run (after pinned wheel): zh-vertical-dev BLEU delta now -0.4 vs r2 (likely noise), chrF -0.008, COMET -0.12.

mei: nice — looks like majority was tokenization. still need to check UR/FA bidi glue issue; bisecting that path now.

liam: for rollout plan: hold r3-int8 until we confirm tokenization parity across packaging and quant compile. also add a localized regression test for stacked-han and mixed-bidi to e2e harness.

mei: agreed. I'll add two test cases to nightly evals and open a small PR to pin tokenizers in the packaging matrix.

sanjay: thanks mei. ping when the bidi repro is bisected.

mei: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
